title: Single-submission Gen1 upgrade receipts and exact-scope observation
summary: upgrade-gen1 requires explicit in-place approval and complete all-ready assessment, sends exactly one guarded POST, preserves acknowledgement/body uncertainty and persists a local scoped receipt. follow-upgrade uses GET-only observation and validates every migration ID/workspace/count; partial/unknown outcomes never authorize retry, grants, mode changes or refresh.
approval: The upgrade is irreversible and cached Gen1 data is not preserved. --allow-in-place-upgrade is a dangerous safety-bypass flag: use it ONLY after explicit approval of the exact IDs and backup/consumer/security review. It does not bypass readiness. No interactive prompt or auto-approve mode exists.

--dry-run validates 1-50 distinct non-zero IDs and previews offline without requiring the approval flag, reading readiness or writing the ledger. Both --readonly and --dry-run remain on previews. Execution under --readonly is refused before reads/writes. --all/--force cannot override readiness, identity or bounds.

Fresh assessment must be complete and all selected items ReadyToMigrate. Defaults: 3 assessment pages, 90 rows including unselected rows, server page size 30. Explicit maxima are 20 pages/600 rows; the API still assesses all workspace Gen1, not an ID-filtered request. Attention/unknown/partial/conflicting evidence blocks before POST.
submission: A TOTAL --timeout (default 120 seconds, maximum 600) bounds readiness, authentication, submission/body reading and optional same-operation waiting. The Fabric sender makes EXACTLY ONE POST, including on 401/429/5xx/network failure. It disables redirect following and never uses response URLs as destinations.

A success acknowledgement survives an unreadable or timed-out body. accepted/acknowledged is not completed migration or refreshed data. Unknown network acceptance is non-retriable; never submit again to obtain an ID. Known request rejection likewise receives no automatic retry.

A unique non-zero x-ms-operation-id is independently authoritative. A different-origin Location is ignored when that header exists; all reads still use the configured client, never that URL. Without the operation header, Location must be an exact configured-origin operations/<UUID> URL. Same-origin identity conflicts, malformed/duplicate headers and normalization tricks suppress identity. x-ms-request-id is only a trace. Endpoint/security routing never switches to a returned origin.

A local receipt UUID and explicit workspace/target scope are persisted BEFORE POST. Before-submission ledger failure fails closed. After-submission persistence failure warns while retaining stdout; it must never turn an accepted operation into a replay. Retain stdout securely for manual recovery if local persistence failed. No credentials, raw API names, messages or returned URLs are stored in the receipt projection.
observation: upgrade-gen1 --wait observes the same verified operation, never resubmits. Without --wait an accepted asynchronous request returns its receipt with completion not_checked. follow-upgrade --receipt-id <LOCAL_RECEIPT_ID> is GET-only: scope is read from that local Gen1 receipt, not latest history or an arbitrary user URL. Receipt endpoint/workspace/IDs are validated; missing or conflicting identity cannot be invented.

--wait uses the acknowledgement Retry-After (capped at 60 seconds) and explicit total timeout plus a 120-attempt cap. GET throttling/retries stay within the remaining budget. Running, malformed, unreadable or unavailable observations do not become completion. No cancellation or timeout-triggered mutation runs.

Only a succeeded operation leads to an operation-result read. Every result must have one row per requested ID, exact workspace, unique identities, recognized statuses, coherent summary counts and matching optional migration operation IDs. Missing/duplicate/wrong-scope/malformed/count-conflicting results remain unknown. Operation failure alone cannot declare every item failed.

Per-item Succeeded/Failed/Unknown outcomes are preserved independently. partial_success and unknown return non-zero with the retained receipt and no retry-safe hint. isRetriable:true is reported evidence, NOT automatic approval or an override of the published 24-hour failed-upgrade cooldown. Never replay a whole partial-success batch.

The local ledger caches sanitized verified results and preserves earlier verified results when later reads fail. Bounded header diagnostics retain a path-token candidate, not URLs or credentials. Follow can recover a unique original operation header rejected solely for Location origin from an accepted 202 receipt, then validates the same result scope. It never uses traces or latest history. GET-only follow updates local bookkeeping only. Preparing/accepted/unknown entries are not pruned; legacy jobs do not invent new identity fields.
not_readiness: Upgrade completion is not first Gen2 refresh, cache/history preservation, destinations, fresh data, working legacy/Viewer consumers, source authorization or rendered reports. No refresh, takeover, permission grant, consumer rewrite, storage/security-mode change or Save As fallback is performed.
